title: Flat scalar extension of integral intermediate total-fraction algebras
statement: Let $A,R$ be reduced commutative rings, let $f:A\to R$ be flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and for any ring $D$ write $Q(D)=S_D^{-1}D$, where $S_D$ is the multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors (elements $s$ satisfying $sx=0\Rightarrow x=0$) [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq Q(A)$ be an integral $A$-subalgebra [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Put $C=R\otimes_A B$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Flatness makes $f(S_A)\subseteq S_R$; write $Q(f):Q(A)\to Q(R)$ for the induced fraction map. Then the formula $j(r\otimes b)=rQ(f)(b)$ defines an injective $R$-algebra map $j:C\hookrightarrow Q(R)$, and $R\to C$ is injective and integral. Via these embeddings the canonical map $Q(C)\to Q(R)$ is an isomorphism. If $C$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $j(C)$ is exactly the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$. Neither $A,R,B,C$ is assumed Noetherian, and $B$ is not assumed finite over $A$. The zero ring is allowed.

source.place: Tags 00HB (definition-flat), 02JK (lemma-base-change-integral), 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed); affine algebra underlying ILO VIII Lemma 2.2.9, printed p.91. Agent generalization of the finite intermediate-algebra comparison lem-trf-flat-birational-normalization-comparison; no single Stacks tag states the whole assertion.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $D$, the localization map $D\to Q(D)$ is injective: if $x/1=0$, [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $v\in S_D$ with $vx=0$, hence $x=0$. If $s\in S_A$, multiplication by $s$ is injective on $A$ and on $B$: on $B\subseteq Q(A)$ it is multiplication by a unit. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] with the flat $A$-module $R$ to these two maps. Under $R\otimes_A A\simeq R$, $r\otimes a\mapsto rf(a)$ (inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$), and on $C=R\otimes_A B$, the resulting maps are multiplication by $f(s)$. Thus $f(s)\in S_R$ and multiplication by $f(s)$ on $C$ is injective. Since $f(S_A)$ consists of units in $Q(R)$, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] gives $Q(f)$, with $Q(f)(a/s)=f(a)/f(s)$.

source.place: Tags 00CM/07JZ (localization construction and kernel), 00HB (definition-flat), 00HD (lemma-flat), 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization). Explicit application to multiplication by a regular element.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] to $R\to Q(R)$ and the restriction $B\to Q(A)\xrightarrow{Q(f)}Q(R)$, which agree on $A$. This constructs a ring map $j:C\to Q(R)$ with $j(r\otimes b)=(r/1)Q(f)(b)$. Let $i:R\to C$ be $r\mapsto r\otimes1$. Then $ji(r)=r/1$, so $j$ is an $R$-algebra map and $i$ is injective by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), bilinearity relations and multiplication on the algebra tensor product; explicit construction from the two compatible algebra maps.

proof.text: We prove injectivity of $j$ without a common denominator for all of $B$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write an arbitrary $c\in C$ as a finite sum $c=\sum_{h=1}^n r_h\otimes b_h$, absorbing any $A$-coefficients into $r_h$. Write $b_h=a_h/t_h$ in $Q(A)$, with $t_h\in S_A$, and put $s=\prod_h t_h$ (empty product $1$). A product of regular elements is regular, since $uvx=0$ implies $vx=0$ and then $x=0$. In $B$ the equality $sb_h=a_h\prod_{k\ne h}t_k\in A$ holds. Tensor balancing therefore gives $f(s)c=i(r_c)$, where $r_c=\sum_h r_h f(a_h\prod_{k\ne h}t_k)\in R$. If $j(c)=0$, applying $j$ gives $r_c/1=0$, whence $r_c=0$ by Step 1. Thus $f(s)c=0$, and the injectivity of multiplication by $f(s)$ on $C$ proved in Step 1 gives $c=0$. Hence $j$ is injective.

source.place: Tags 00CX (lemma-tensor-product: pure tensors generate and balancing relations) and 00CM/07JZ (fraction representation). Explicit finite-sum denominator calculation; the two injectivity inputs were established in Step 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change] to $A\to B$ and $A\to R$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed integral extension and the given ring map, and its structure map is $i(r)=r\otimes1$. Thus $R\to C$ is integral. Step 2 already proved that it is injective.

Identify $R\subseteq C\subseteq Q(R)$ using $i,j$. For $u\in S_R$, multiplication by $u$ on $C$ is injective, since $u$ is a unit in $Q(R)$; thus $u\in S_C$. Conversely take $t\in S_C$ and write $j(t)=r/u$ in $Q(R)$ with $r\in R$, $u\in S_R$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Injectivity of $j$ gives $ut=r$ in $C$. If $rx=0$ for $x\in R$, then $t(ux)=0$ in $C$, hence $ux=0$ by regularity of $t$, and $x=0$ by regularity of $u$ and injectivity of $R\to C$. Therefore $r\in S_R$. It follows that $j(t)=r/u$ is a unit of $Q(R)$, with inverse $u/r$.

source.place: Tags 00CM/07JZ (fraction representation and multiplication); explicit regular-denominator argument for the intermediate ring, with the embeddings supplied in Steps 2--3.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property], Step 5 lets $j$ extend to $J:Q(C)\to Q(R)$ and $R\to C\to Q(C)$ extend to $H:Q(R)\to Q(C)$. The composite $JH$ is the identity because it agrees on $R$. For $c\in C$ write $j(c)=r/u$ with $u\in S_R$. Then $uc=i(r)$ by injectivity of $j$, and $i(u)\in S_C$ by Step 5. Consequently $HJ(c/1)=H(r/u)=i(r)/i(u)=c/1$. The two maps $HJ$ and $1_{Q(C)}$ therefore agree on $C$, so localization uniqueness gives $HJ=1$. Thus the canonical $J$, characterized by $J(c/t)=j(c)j(t)^{-1}$, is an isomorphism compatible with the given embeddings.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), existence, fraction formula and uniqueness; explicit verification of both inverse composites.

proof.text: Assume now that $C$ is normal. Step 4 and [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] put $j(C)$ inside the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$: apply $j$ to a monic equation for each $c\in C$. Conversely let $x\in Q(R)$ satisfy a monic equation over $R$. Apply $H$ to that equation; its coefficients are the images in $C$ of the coefficients in $R$, so $H(x)\in Q(C)$ is integral over $C$. The hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] holds for this $C$, so $H(x)=c/1$ for some $c\in C$. Applying $J$ gives $x=j(c)$. This proves the required equality of subrings. Every preceding argument also works when a ring is zero: regularity means injective multiplication, the localization and tensor universal properties allow the zero ring, and neither a prime nor a nonzero element was chosen.

source.place: Tags 00GI/00GP (integral equations and integral closure), 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed). Explicit transfer of the monic equation along the inverse total-fraction isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem flat_integral_totalFractions (A : Type u) (R : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [IsReduced A] [IsReduced R] [Algebra A R] (hf : (algebraMap A R).Flat) (B : Subalgebra A (FractionRing A)) [Algebra.IsIntegral A B] : ∃ hregular : nonZeroDivisors A ≤ (nonZeroDivisors R).comap (algebraMap A R), ∃ j : R ⊗[A] B →ₐ[R] FractionRing R, (∀ (r : R) (b : B), j (r ⊗ₜ[A] b) = algebraMap R (FractionRing R) r * IsLocalization.map (FractionRing R) (algebraMap A R) hregular (b : FractionRing A)) ∧ Function.Injective j ∧ Function.Injective (algebraMap R (R ⊗[A] B)) ∧ Algebra.IsIntegral R (R ⊗[A] B) ∧ (∃ e : FractionRing (R ⊗[A] B) ≃+* FractionRing R, ∀ c : R ⊗[A] B, e (algebraMap (R ⊗[A] B) (FractionRing (R ⊗[A] B)) c) = j c) ∧ ((∀ (p : Ideal (R ⊗[A] B)) [p.IsPrime], IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) → j.range = integralClosure R (FractionRing R))
